conceptual assets.information: The register file holds architectural operand values that CPU execution depends on, receives write-back data, and returns selected source operands. The contents enter through rd_i and leave through the operand output ports.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The register contents may contain private or security-sensitive CPU data and are exposed through rs1_o, rs2_o and rs3_o at lines 88-89, 126-127 and 141. The contents can be changed by rd_i writes at lines 86 and 110 and cleared or fixed by the reset and constant assignments at lines 107 and 117.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who influences the write-back path or the register-file storage can read register values through the operand outputs or replace values used by later CPU operations.

conceptual assets.information: The write-target selection determines which register receives write-back data, so register-file updates depend on it. It is derived from the control record and is consumed internally rather than returned through an output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the write-target selection can redirect rd_i to an unintended register, as the selection controls opa_addr and register writes at lines 78-79, 86 and 109.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who alters the register-select or write-control fields can redirect a write-back value into a different architectural register.

conceptual assets.information: The read-source selection determines which register value is supplied as each source operand, and CPU execution depends on those selected operands. It is derived from ctrl_i and is consumed internally to select the values returned on the operand outputs.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the read-source selection can substitute a different register value for an operand, through the indexed reads and output assignments at lines 89, 126-127 and 141.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who changes the source-register selections can cause the CPU to operate on unintended register values or expose a different register value on an operand output.

conceptual assets.information: The zero-register protection decision suppresses ordinary writes to register zero, preserving the architectural constant-zero behavior on which CPU instruction semantics depend. The decision is computed from the control record and has no independent output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The rd_zero comparison and write-enable logic protect register zero from ordinary updates at lines 76-77, while the ASIC implementation excludes index zero from the write processes and drives it to zero at lines 109 and 117. The rf_zero_we override selects address zero and permits a write at lines 77-78 and 86, which can make later operand outputs incorrect at lines 88 and 126.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who asserts or corrupts the zero-write override path can change register zero and cause subsequent instructions to receive a nonzero value where the architecture expects zero.

considered, not kept.reason: The rf_rd, rf_rs1, rf_rs2, rf_wb_en, rf_zero_we and ir_funct12 fields only specify access direction, register selection or write enable, so the access-command-fields rule bars them as a separate conceptual asset.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset register-file storage and output registers, and the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
RST_EN, RVE_EN and RS3_EN only select the implementation, register-file size or optional read port at build time and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
